newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sonaca new restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sonaca new restructuring plan.

text.p: Belgian aeronautical firm Sonaca SA said on Thursday that increased work meant it needed to speed up production changes and restructuring in the next two years.

New orders for Airbus A-320 parts are more than 60 percent higher than expected for 1997 and more than 100 percent higher for 1998, Sonaca managing director Christian Jacquemin told Reuters. He said new parts orders for the 50 seat Brazilian Embrayer aircraft were also much higher than expected.
"We need to double activity in our major programmes in the next two years," Jacquemin said.
He said a new restructuring plan was presented to the Board on Thursday, but declined to say if the increased workload would affect plans to shed 479 of 1,130 staff over the next three years.

"The sharp increase in orders obliges us to look for additional staff, but it's important to remember that this is a cyclical industry and we must keep a competitive structure," said Jacquemin. Sonaca's 92 percent shareholder, the Walloon region government, invested 600 million francs in the company last March.
